The Arch Angels

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The are a group of unlikely seafarers brought together by fate ,they are the Arch Angels and they are taking the world of sailing by storm.

Unique Selling Point:
- In a history-making voyage, the first complete crew
from the Royal Cape Yacht Club Sailing Academy hailing from marginalised communities
has crossed the finish line of the 50 th Cape2Rio yacht race, after a thrilling battle to gain third
position.
The dreams of five young South Africans came true on Thursday as their boat, the
AArchAngel, arrived in Rio de Janeiro after 24 days and a 3,300 nautical mile
ocean crossing from Cape Town to Guanabara Bay.
Skipper Sibusiso Sizatu (30), first mate Daniel Agulhas (29), Renaldo Tshepo Mohale (29),
Azile Arosi (22) and Justin Peters (21) departed on January 2, with the backdrop of the
historic Robben Island reminding them of Nelson Mandela’s words, "It always
seems impossible until it's done”.
The final hours of ArchAngel’s race saw the boat neck and neck with their closest
competitor, Argonaut, eventually beating them by 23 minutes.
This is the achievement of their lives. So many years, so many obstacles, yet they kept
moving forward.
Born into disadvantaged communities, the crew have broken stereotypes of race and class
and demonstrated that it is possible for people from diverse backgrounds to participate in
sports such as yachting, previously accessible only to the privileged few.
Sizatu says in the future, he hopes to see an all-female crew from the Academy doing a race
of similar stature, empowering more women in the sport.
The Alexforbes ArchAngel crew have made history in the golden anniversary of the iconic
race. Sixteen teams lined up at the start, hailing from South Africa, Brazil, India, Italy and the
United States of America, with three boats withdrawing during the challenging event. The
overall race was won by Atalanta, with Ray of Light in second position.

Script: Arch Angels

Opening scene: [fade out of black …slow visuals of the sunrise over Muizenberg beach… Ethereal music and the splashing of waves can be heard. We see visuals of a figure…Sibu is standing on the shore looking out]

Upsound Sibusiso: The ocean is a thing of beauty…

Upsound Sibusiso: Also to be respected…

Upsound Sibusiso: When I set sail, its as if nothing else in the world matters.

Upsound Sibusiso: Many have tried to conquer it and failed…



2.V/O Over six thousand kilometres from Cape Town…across treacherous oceans to Rio de Janeiro in Brazil…the legendary Cape2Rio Yacht Race is one of the most gruelling on the planet… attracting some of the world’s best sailors.


3. V/O Every other year, since 1971, the race has taken those brave enough to enter across the unforgiving South Atlantic Ocean… it’s why it attracts only the most skilled, most experienced sailors.

4.V/O This year, though, was…well…a little different.

News report audio: young people from Masiphumelele, Khayelitsha, Grassy Park and Athlone are making history…They are taking part in the Cape to Rio yacht race.

5.V/O The 2023 edition attracted an unlikely group of seafarers - the youngest and first full crew from marginalised communities across the Western Cape. Products of the Royal Cape Yacht Club Sailing Academy, they’re called “The Alexforbes Arch Angels”.

Nat sound: “Coming down, coming down…jibe, jibe.”

6.Link Mac: Sailing is considered an elitist sport, only for the privileged few, but I will be spending time with youth from rural Qumbu in the Eastern Cape, all the way to the Cape Flats that are changing that perception.

7. V/O It’s unlikely any of the other crews in the race had encountered life challenges on the scale of this 5-person team. But what they lack in experience, they make up for in enthusiasm.

Upsound Azile (18:40):I was a bit nervous because I'd never crossed an ocean before. It was going to be my first time sailing from one country to another.I didn't even know what to expect out there.

8. V/O The crew’s captain is Sibusiso Sizatu. It’s an unexpected role for someone born in landlocked Qumbu in the Eastern Cape.
Macfarlane question (01:19):And in your mind, did you ever think you'd end up here working on sailboats and eventually sailing the trans-Atlantic?
Upsound Sibusisio Sizatu (01:31)I never thought I would be a sailor. So I mean the first time I saw the ocean was here, 2003 and I just see this big thing keep coming towards me. I was like, oh, this is strange.
9. V/O Sibusiso first encountered sailing after moving to Cape Town’s Masiphumelele township in 2005, after an NGO introduced the sport into local townships. It was an alien world far removed from the grind of his daily existence.
Upsound Sibusisio Sizatu (05:28) I went to try it out and then they put me on the boat I got sea sick I got car sick so I was like This is not for me. So I stayed away back to soccer.
10. V/O But watching his friends who stuck to it travelling the country, attending races, forced a re-think.
Upsound: Sibusiso (06:55):So in 2007 I went again and So now one guy needed a crew and yeah I am sitting there and then I was told, go back home, go pack your bags, you're going to Mossel Bay.I don't even know how to sail. I don't even know how to pull a rope. So I sailed with him and we came third .standing there watching the crowd clapping hands for you. That's amazing.
VO: Turns out, he was a natural! (PAUSE)
11.V/O Sibusiso’s rise was dramatic, going on to represent South Africa at sailing championships around the world. (PAUSE) But, he harboured a single dream: testing his mettle in the iconic Cape2Rio… with a crew of only emerging sailors.
Upsound Sibusiso : (25:47) I found myself talking about Rio.
12. V/O The Cape to Rio is a test of courage as well as endurance: the seas in this part of the world are notoriously temperamental - home to the ominous Roaring 40’s and Furious 50’s latitudes. Crews have to navigate swells as high as 10 meters and more…battling wind speeds of over a hundred kilometres an hour.
UPS NATSOUND / BREATHE
13. V/O Azile Arosi grew up in Khayelitsha, never expecting that - like her captain, Sibusiso - sailing would change her life.
Upsound Azile (03:30):Oh my word. First of all, I knew nothing about sailing growing up froEven when I got here, I knew nothing about sailing
Upsound Azile (06:02):they took us for swimming lessons and then from swimming So we started sailing on dinghies, getting to know how the boat works and parts of the boat. And then after four, six months, if I'm not mistaken, from there we came to the bigger boats
14. V/O Sailing is highly technical, demanding physical strength…balance… patience…and teamwork. Azile wasn’t fazed by being the only female on the crew.
Upsound Azile: (09:59): We were so excited and we were like, .there's a lot to do that we need to do. Being the only girl on the boat. For me it wasn't, wasn't like, how can I say it? I'm so used to the guys. I've been sailing with the guys for more than three years now. So even at home, back at home, I grew up with guys.I feel like a bigger person even though I'm so thin.
15.V/O Justin Peters is the youngest member of the team. Hailing from the gang and drug-ridden Cape Flats.
Upsound : Justin (13:13):The friends that I have, some of, them took the wrong path and some of them of them lost their lives also.
16 .V/O sailing offers him refuge… an escape.
Upsound Justin(04:17):It's my first time me leaving the country or so yeah. So it was just perfect. Everything was perfect. Exciting and yeah.//(05:13). We done training for the race but you can't train yourself enough. You have to go and do the race to actually get into it.
17. V/O For all their heart, this team lacks resources… and sailing is an expensive pastime. Their dreams of competing on a global stage hinged on finding financial backing. It came at the very last minute.
Upsound Sibusiso S (27:55):Now to prepare to go to Rio, you need at least two years on the boat just sorting out about two years. And then that needs money.
Upsound Azile :(09:59): Still we could find sponsors, we got the sponsor around May, June, may or June. That's when we got the sponsor and it was, were way too late because we still need to prepare boat and all that stuff. There's a lot to do before you do this. The race. So we got the sponsor like six months before the race. So we were so excited first of all because wow, the previous Rio, we were so disappointed we didn't get a sponsor. And now we got a sponsor very late. But still, we were so excited and we were like, we wanted to do this. We didn't care about the fact that we got it very late and there's a l that we need to do. So we were so excited.
[breather /bridge]
18. V/O After years of planning, training, and dreaming, it’s race day!!… Family and friends gather… excited… anxious.
Upsound Azile (18:40):First day the start of the race was at 2:00 PM and then we started the race. It was going to be my first time sailing from one country to another. Upsound Justin: (07:56) Just looking at everyone there and the day that is finally the time we've been training for practising all of that, all the work, putting our time in and all of that. The day has finally arrived.
19. V/O A pulsating start… the Arch Angels keeping pace with the leading boats as Cape Town disappears behind them…

20. V/O But after just 3 days … trouble strikes, threatening to end their race and crush their dreams.
Macfarlane Question (28:24): What was the moment that you felt like you were in trouble here?
Upsound Azile (28:36): the scariest moment is when Sibu told us the rudder was broken. Cause once Thera is broken it's game over because there's nothing else you can do
[ breather]
21. V/O If it broke completely, the yacht would veer off course - the crew helpless to intervene… at the mercy of the Atlantic and the currents. (PAUSE) Panicked, Sibusiso radioed for help.
[ breather]
Upsound Sibu at sea:It gave us a bit of panic and then we called in on the radio, for us to start to kind of give us information, how can we start it out?:And the guy said, okay, we need to go to Walvis Bay in Namibia and stop there. But the problem with that, if we stop there, we get [ mac noddy] disqualified for him from the race.
22. The crew had a decision to make.
[ longer Breather]
Upsound Sibu at sea :(01:22): What came out the team is that we didn't enter the race to stop somewhere. Yeah. Let sail the boat until the rudder breaks. So we came up with that solution and we carry on going.
[breather to create tension]
23 V/O Now a full two days behind the leading boats, in 11th place, and facing seemingly hopeless odds, Sibusiso’s crew showed their mettle. Determined to fight, they knuckled down, valiantly battling rough seas and unpredictable winds for 20 days.
Upsound Justin07:00):Just getting there coming to Rio would be the reward on itself. And that's what kept us going. And knowing our support team behind us. all with our families, our friends. Yeah, just kept going. That's why retiring wasn't really an option for us.
[ Action sequence, crew sailing , turbulent seas]
24. V/O A moment of triumph: on the 26th of January, the AlexForbes ArchAngels emerged on the horizon , off South America… They had made it all the way to Rio de Janeiro. Having made up 8 places, they finished a remarkable 3rd out of 16 competing crews.
Upsound : Azile (22:06):Oh wait, you should have seen us on the okay. The day. Oh we're so tired. Okay. When we got there, the day we knew that we were going to finish I think on the We were like, the crowd was going besides us . It was like, like we won the first place even though we didn't even know that we got the podium finfinished the race, we crossed the finish line despite of everything that was happening on the potent, being tired, oh my word. It was just an amazing experience.
Upsound Sibusiso: (05:17) What I saw around the team at that moment is that we holding each other together.
Upsound Justin:Speaker 3 (10:07):. Making podium position was just like, cause if you look, four of us on the boat has never done the Rio race has never crossed the Atlantic Ocean t. Yeah, we done it in 23 days with people that's been doing the Rio race a couple of times beating them.
25. V/O A crew brought together by circumstance… battling the odds together…The ArchAngels have cast stereotypes aside and become yet another example to a nation in desperate need of heroes.
[end]

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The are a group of unlikely seafarers brought together by fate ,they are the Arch Angels and they are taking the world of sailing by storm.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: - In a history-making voyage, the first complete crew from the Royal Cape Yacht Club Sailing Academy hailing from marginalised communities has crossed the finish line of the 50 th Cape2Rio yacht race, after a thrilling battle to gain third position. The dreams of five young South Africans came true on Thursday as their boat, the AArchAngel, arrived in Rio de Janeiro after 24 days and a 3,300 nautical mile ocean crossing from Cape Town to Guanabara Bay. Skipper Sibusiso Sizatu (30), first mate Daniel Agulhas (29), Renaldo Tshepo Mohale (29), Azile Arosi (22) and Justin Peters (21) departed on January 2, with the backdrop of the historic Robben Island reminding them of Nelson Mandela’s words, "It always seems impossible until it's done”. The final hours of ArchAngel’s race saw the boat neck and neck with their closest competitor, Argonaut, eventually beating them by 23 minutes. This is the achievement of their lives. So many years, so many obstacles, yet they kept moving forward. Born into disadvantaged communities, the crew have broken stereotypes of race and class and demonstrated that it is possible for people from diverse backgrounds to participate in sports such as yachting, previously accessible only to the privileged few. Sizatu says in the future, he hopes to see an all-female crew from the Academy doing a race of similar stature, empowering more women in the sport. The Alexforbes ArchAngel crew have made history in the golden anniversary of the iconic race. Sixteen teams lined up at the start, hailing from South Africa, Brazil, India, Italy and the United States of America, with three boats withdrawing during the challenging event. The overall race was won by Atalanta, with Ray of Light in second position.
